title: FAQ - Better Resource Monitor
description: How GPU monitoring works, resource usage, privacy, and how it compares to Stats and iStat Menus.
heading: FAQ

items.question: What is Better Resource Monitor?
items.answer: A free, open-source menu bar app that shows CPU, memory, GPU, and network usage on macOS. Written in Rust. Under 0.1% CPU and about 15 MB of RAM.

items.question: Which macOS versions has it been tested on?
items.answer: It has been tested on Intel Macs running macOS Ventura and on the latest macOS Sonoma release.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes. MIT-licensed, no paid tiers, no in-app purchases. The Mac App Store and GitHub versions are the same app.

items.question: How much CPU and memory does it use?
items.answer: Under 0.1% CPU and about 15 MB of RAM on an Apple M1. For comparison, Stats uses ~50 MB and iStat Menus uses 100+ MB. The app binary is under 7 MB.

items.question: How does GPU monitoring work?
items.answer: On macOS, it reads device utilization from Apple Silicon GPUs through Apple's public IOAccelerator API. No private APIs, no sudo. Both the App Store and GitHub versions include GPU monitoring.

items.question: Does it collect any data?
items.answer: No. Zero network requests, no analytics, no telemetry. Everything stays on your machine. The source code is on GitHub if you want to verify that yourself.

items.question: How does it compare to iStat Menus and Stats?
items.answer: All three show system metrics in the menu bar. The differences: Stats needs a root helper for fan and thermal data. iStat Menus costs $14.99 and also needs root. Better Resource Monitor runs entirely in user space, uses about 15 MB of RAM, and is free. See the [Stats comparison page]({{vsStatsUrl}}) and [iStat Menus comparison page]({{vsIstatMenusUrl}}) for details.

items.question: Does it drain MacBook battery?
items.answer: No. Monitors that poll fans and thermal sensors keep Apple Silicon from entering deep sleep. This app skips those readings entirely, which is why it sits under 0.1% CPU.

items.question: Why not just use Activity Monitor?
items.answer: Activity Monitor is a full window you have to open. This lives in your menu bar and updates every second. You see the numbers without switching apps.
